Feature: Replace static ExternalSecrets with operator projection

# GitHub Issue #443: feat(c5c3-operator): replace the remaining static ExternalSecrets (keystone-admin, mariadb-root-password, k-orc-clouds-yaml) with operator-owned projection

**Description:**

`deploy/eso/externalsecrets/` still ships three statically applied ExternalSecrets — `keystone-admin.yaml`, `mariadb-root-password.yaml`, and `k-orc-clouds-yaml.yaml`, all listed in `deploy/eso/kustomization.yaml` and pulled into the production stack via `deploy/flux-system/infrastructure/kustomization.yaml:23` (`- ../../eso`). Each pins the default Quick Start identity (ControlPlane `controlplane` in namespace `openstack`), so bringing up a ControlPlane under any other name or namespace requires editing static manifests. This issue gives them the CC-0116 treatment that PR #442 (commit `407e8580`) established for `keystone-db`: operator-owned per-ControlPlane projection where a per-CR credential exists, production deletion plus a kind-only shim where only the standalone/dev flow needs the default identity, and outright consumer elimination where the manifest backs nothing on the critical path.

The work splits into one operator feature (Secret 1, the bulk of the change), one manifest relocation (Secret 2), and one consumer removal (Secret 3). The concrete boundaries:

**1. The structural template already exists; this issue adds its admin-password sibling.**

<commit-best-practices>
<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0117): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>

<git-identity>
  <rule name="author">ALWAYS use --author flag: git commit --author "Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>" -m "..."</rule>

  <rule name="trailers">Append these trailers at the end of the commit message body, separated by a blank line:
    AI-assisted: Claude Code
    On-behalf-of: @SAP christian.berendt@sap.com
    Signed-off-by: Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>
  </rule>
</git-identity>
